subject: Security discovery: console telemetry / vendor SQ next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Thomas <julie.thomas@medisoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security discovery: console telemetry / vendor SQ next steps

Hi Julie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we stay aligned: 

- SOC 2 status: Redwood is currently in-scope for SOC 2 Type II reporting; our last audit completed May 2025 (summary attached). Full report can be shared under NDA if you need the auditor letter.
- GDPR/HIPAA posture: We support data residency controls (US/EU regions) and offer BAA for customers with PHI needs; we discussed high-level controls on encryption at-rest and in-transit.
- Console telemetry & cookies: you asked specifically what we collect on the customer Console and public docs site. High level: first-party analytics for product usage (page view counts, route-level latency aggregates), performance telemetry (client-side metrics to measure SDK / API latency), and error logging. We do not embed cross-site third-party trackers for behavioral advertising. Detailed breakdown below and in the attached short doc:
  * Console: first-party session cookie (session_id) to maintain UI sessions; a first-party analytics cookie (r_analytics) with a 90-day TTL for aggregated usage metrics; no persistent PII in cookies.
  * Docs site: lightweight first-party analytics for page views and docs search trends, opt-out via the footer link.
  * Telemetry sent with requests: request metadata (model id, region, token counts, latency) used for billing and performance; customer-provided prompt/content is not stored beyond retention unless explicitly enabled for quality monitoring (opt-in).

Proposed next steps: 
1) You send over the vendor security questionnaire (or we can pull it from your vendor portal).
2) We complete the questionnaire and return within 2 business days; attach SOC 2 summary and controls mapping.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our Product Security lead and an engineer to walk through telemetry fields, retention windows, and optional opt-outs (30–60 mins).

Can you confirm the right person for the questionnaire (security@medisoft.com or a different contact) and a preferred time window for the deep-dive later this week?

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — that summary is helpful. I've attached our standard vendor security questionnaire (VDD) — it's a compact worksheet (about 40 questions). Mike (cc'd) will own the technical review.

Proposed timeline: if you can return the completed questionnaire by end-of-day Thursday (11/6), that would keep us on track for procurement next week. For the deep-dive, we prefer afternoon PST on Thursday.

Julie Thomas
Head of IT Risk | Medisoft Health
julie.thomas@medisoft.com | 415-212-9981

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Thomas <julie.thomas@medisoft.com>, Mike Gunter <security@medisoft.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, dev_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security discovery: console telemetry / vendor SQ next steps

Julie / Mike —

Appreciate the questionnaire — we'll start filling it out today. Quick answers to Julie's point so you have something immediate for procurement: 

- Prompt/content persistence: by default, hosted API customers' request+response data is retained for 30 days and is not used for model training. Customers can opt into longer retention or data-sharing for quality & fine-tuning; in that case we require explicit consent and contractual terms. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customer content does not leave the customer's environment unless they choose to enable managed backups.
- Access controls & encryption: all customer data at-rest is encrypted with customer-managed KMS option for enterprise accounts; in-transit uses TLS 1.2+.
- Telemetry details: the telemetry payload includes model identifier, token counts (input/output), request latency, region, error codes, and a hashed request id for deduplication. It does not include raw prompt text unless the customer has enabled "detailed logging" for support, which is auditable and time-limited.
- Cookies & docs tracking: we only use first-party cookies; third-party trackers (advertising pixels) are not present on the console. Our docs site uses a consent banner and honors do-not-track for the lightweight analytics.

Attachments: I've attached a completed SQ draft (medisoft_vendor_sq_v1_filled.pdf) with inline references to our SOC 2 summary and the controls mapping; also attached the SOC 2 summary PDF. We'll also propose a 45-minute deep-dive slot on Thursday at 1:30pm PST (invite to follow from Lauren).

If Mike needs a technical owner from our side for the deep-dive, that'll be Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwoodinference.com).

Best,
Soojin

Attachments: medisoft_vendor_sq_v1_filled.pdf (PDF, 150KB); redwood_soc2_status_summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks — that answers most of our immediate questions and the timeline works. A couple of follow-ups for the deep-dive: 

1) HIPAA: can you confirm what fields are redacted by default (names, MRNs, any PHI) and whether Redwood will sign a BAA before we share PHI in a test environment?
2) Retention configuration: for hosted customers, is the 30-day retention configurable per-account via the Console, or is it a contract-time configuration only?

I'll wait for the completed SQ and the calendar invite.

-Mike
